enhanced_information: In Diabetes insipidus, there is a deficiency of antidiuretic hormone (ADH) or a resistance to its effects, leading to impaired water reabsorption in the kidneys. This results in the production of large volumes of dilute urine. The standard consensus indicates that urine osmolality in Diabetes insipidus is typically less than 300 mmol/L, often around 100-200 mmol/L, reflecting the inability to concentrate urine. Therefore, the most accurate option is <300 mmol/L. The reasoning chains indicating urine osmolality <150 mmol/L and <600 mmol/L are misleading, as they do not accurately represent the typical osmolality seen in this condition. analysis: In Diabetes insipidus, the primary issue is the inability to concentrate urine due to a deficiency of antidiuretic hormone (ADH) or resistance to its effects. This leads to the production of large volumes of dilute urine. The typical urine osmolality in this condition is less than 300 mmol/L, often falling within the range of 100-200 mmol/L.
